# Didache Chapter 15 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Hierosolymitanus (H), Didache 15 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/DID_015_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 15

**1** Therefore appoint for yourselves bishops and deacons worthy of the Lord — men who are meek and not lovers of money and true and tested; for they also minister to you the ministry of the prophets and teachers.

**2** Therefore do not despise them — for they are the ones who are honored among you along with the prophets and teachers.

**3** And reprove one another not in anger but in peace, as you have it in the gospel; and let no one speak to any who has wronged his neighbor, nor let him hear from you, until he has repented.

**4** But your prayers and your almsgiving and all your deeds, do them as you have it in the gospel of our Lord.

---

*EMET notes: V.1 — "bishops and deacons" (ἐπισκόπους καὶ διακόνους) — this is the earliest non-Pauline reference to the bishop-deacon structure (cf. Phil 1:1; 1 Tim 3). Notably, no "elders" (πρεσβύτεροι) are mentioned. "Tested" (δεδοκιμασμένους) = proven, examined and approved. V.1-2 — bishops and deacons are presented as the local settled ministry that supplements (and gradually replaces) the itinerant prophets and teachers. V.3 — "reprove in peace" = community discipline is to be done without anger. "Let no one speak to" = a form of social/liturgical exclusion for the unrepentant (cf. Matt 18:15-17). V.4 — "the gospel of our Lord" (τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν) — a written document is clearly in view.*
